title: Efficient ATT Estimation with Replicate Measurements of an Error-Prone Confounder
banked_reason: formalization needs massive missing infrastructure (spline oracle inequality, Fourier bias/variance and fold-moment bounds, inverse-gradient stability, cutoff asymptotics, activeSetQP_*, exactSplineFit_exists, cosine_multiplier, marked_representation); discovery math NOT refuted (D0.5 field PASS)
gap_reasons: The proof needs a certified risk bound for this spline quadratic program and inverse-score coupling. Causalean concept, type, and goal searches, local searches, and Mathlib search found only general projection or unrelated risk lemmas; those do not establish the solver-specific bounds.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery passed D0.5 at field tier, and the Lean run proved the induced-law ModelClass certificate plus four projected-risk helper lemmas without added axioms. F3 stopped at projected_inverse_risk because a spline oracle inequality, Fourier and fold-moment bounds, inverse-gradient stability, cutoff asymptotics, and several upstream solver and representation theorems remain unproved. The discovery mathematics was not refuted; formalization needs massive missing infrastructure.
tldr: Repeated Gaussian measurements of an error-prone confounder recover the clean-confounder ATT efficiency benchmark exactly when \(p_n\log n/\sqrt n\to\infty\). Above this frontier, a fully observable finite spline quadratic-program spectral one-step procedure attains the clean variance; its observable variance estimate has a uniformly integrable square root, which yields a uniformly honest Wald interval with clean-benchmark expected length. Below the frontier, for each disclosed repeat plan and finite frontier cap, one fixed legal compact-support pair is chosen before selecting any bounded-frontier subsequence; the same pair has a nonzero root-\(n\) ATT gap and one-record observed chi-square divergence \(o(n^{-1})\) along every such subsequence. In the polynomial first non-clean regime, the legal marked-density modulus has common uniform order \((p_n\log n)^{-1}\); its sharp constant, optimizer, limit experiment, and matching estimator and interval remain open.
gap: Published causal methods either assume the confounder is observed or correct error-prone-covariate weighting and matching at the level of identification or consistency without quantifying when repeated measurements restore the clean ATT efficiency bound. Repeated-measurement deconvolution establishes first-order equivalence between unknown-error and known-error density or regression estimators under fixed bounded replication, but published inverse-problem methods do not handle ATT's ratio of four marked densities, a growing known-Gaussian repeat count, an unknown sum density, and causal legality constraints.
fill: The project pairs an explicit projected spectral one-step upper construction with a compact-support same-class lower pair and then formulates the first non-clean precision loss as a computable legal marked-density modulus.
